extensions.themeStrategy: Light default in the frontmatter is normative. Dark is a :root token swap under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) — no per-component overrides, no in-app toggle. `dark` below is the dark-mode value of each token.

display.purpose: The one big line per screen. Weight 400, never bolder.

title.purpose: A card's own heading. First place weight 500 appears.

reply.purpose: Signature style: Gabay's replies in the thread, larger and looser than a bubble.

caption.purpose: Dense sub-body tier (0.78-0.95rem, centered on 0.88): card reason lines, contact labels, trust line, timestamps, the ack status line, the Case panel title.

label.purpose: Rail headings, eyebrows, quiet metadata. Small but weight 500.

shadows.name: xs
shadows.purpose: Faintest lift: opener chips, language select, claim rows, icon-button hover.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Default floating surface: cards, calm emergency pill, quiet buttons, the Case panel (side card).

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: The composer, the hover state of an sm surface, and the Case panel when it drops as a sheet on a narrow screen.

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs and the toast only.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible on every interactive element, offset 3px.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default for box-shadow / background / color state changes on controls.

motion.name: glow-fade
motion.purpose: The .ph-glow layer animating to 0 once the thread has a message.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: The three loader dots — auth screen, screen transitions, and the loading animation under the transcript while a reply streams.

motion.name: case-panel-reveal
motion.purpose: The Case panel body fading and rising in on expand; chevron rotates 0.18s. Height snaps, no layout property is animated. Instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Brand Lockup
components.description: The hand-and-path mark beside the wordmark — the rail, the mobile topbar, the welcome nav, the loading screen. Sized by height (the artwork is 1.22:1), never width; pine on either ground.
components.css: .ds-brand { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.55rem; color: var(--ink, #1f1f1f); font-family: Figtree, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-brand-mark { height: 1.85rem; width: calc(1.85rem * 39.09 / 32); color: var(--pine, #1f5e4a); flex-shrink: 0; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Confirm / commit action. Pine fill, no shadow — it sits in the page rather than floating.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:.5rem; background:#1f5e4a; color:#fff; font:500 .95rem 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; padding:.8rem 1.4rem; border:none; border-radius:999px; cursor:pointer; transition:background .14s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#163f32; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid rgba(31,94,74,.35); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: The default button. White pill that floats on the ground; hover raises the shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:.5rem; background:#fff; color:#1f1f1f; font:500 .95rem 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; padding:.8rem 1.4rem; border:none; border-radius:999px; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,31,31,.08),0 6px 18px rgba(31,31,31,.06); transition:box-shadow .14s ease; } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,31,31,.08),0 12px 34px rgba(31,31,31,.08); } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline:3px solid rgba(31,94,74,.35); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Composer
components.description: The floating white pill that never leaves the screen. Two matched circular buttons — an add-a-photo control at the head, send at the tail — flank a borderless auto-growing textarea, optically centred against a single line of text. The send glyph takes pine once the field has text. Enter sends; Shift+Enter is a newline.

components.css: .ds-composer { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:.3rem; background:var(--surface,#fff); border-radius:32px; box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,31,31,.08),0 12px 34px rgba(31,31,31,.08); padding:.4rem .5rem; max-width:47rem; width:100%; } .ds-composer-plus, .ds-composer-send { flex-shrink:0; width:2.5rem; height:2.5rem; border:none; background:none; border-radius:50%; display:grid; place-items:center; color:var(--muted,#6e7370); cursor:pointer; transition:background .14s ease, color .14s ease; } .ds-composer-plus svg, .ds-composer-send svg { width:1.2rem; height:1.2rem; display:block; } .ds-composer-plus:hover, .ds-composer-send:hover { background:var(--faint,#f1f1ee); color:var(--ink,#1f1f1f); } .ds-composer-input { flex:1; min-width:0; border:none; resize:none; background:none; padding:.6rem .2rem; max-height:8rem; font:400 1rem/1.5 Figtree,system-ui,-apple-system,'Segoe UI',sans-serif; color:var(--ink,#1f1f1f); caret-color:var(--pine,#1f5e4a); } .ds-composer-input::placeholder { color:var(--muted,#6e7370); } .ds-composer-input:focus { outline:none; } .ds-composer-input:not(:placeholder-shown) + .ds-composer-send { color:var(--pine,#1f5e4a); } .ds-composer-send:disabled { opacity:.4; cursor:default; } .ds-composer-plus:focus-visible, .ds-composer-send:focus-visible { outline:3px solid rgba(31,94,74,.35); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: User Chat Bubble
components.description: The visitor's own chat turn. A warm grey, deliberately quieter than a saturated sent-message blue; right-aligned.
components.html: About sixteen. Six in the morning until ten at night.
components.css: .ds-bubble-user { align-self:flex-end; max-width:32rem; background:#efeeec; color:#1f1f1f; font:400 1rem/1.55 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; padding:.85rem 1.2rem; border-radius:20px; }

components.name: Agent Reply
components.description: Gabay's reply in the thread. No bubble, no card — the rotated pine square, then markless prose set larger and looser than a bubble.
components.html: Your contract says eight hours a day. On a normal day, how many hours do you really work?
components.css: .ds-agent-reply { align-self:flex-start; max-width:40rem; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:.7rem; color:#1f1f1f; font:400 1.08rem/1.62 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; } .ds-agent-reply::before { content:''; width:.95rem; height:.95rem; border-radius:4px; background:#1f5e4a; transform:rotate(45deg); }

components.name: Loading Animation
components.description: The whole of the in-flight feedback while a reply streams: three pulsing pine dots where the reply will land, left-aligned in the thread. Replaces the old visible Progress Trail text (the backend still emits code-owned trail labels; the client no longer renders them). Clears the instant the reply arrives. Freezes to a static dimmed row under prefers-reduced-motion.
components.css: .ds-typing { align-self:flex-start; display:flex; flex-direction:row; gap:.35rem; align-items:center; } .ds-typing span { width:.5rem; height:.5rem; border-radius:50%; background:#1f5e4a; animation:ds-pulse 1.1s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-typing span:nth-child(2) { animation-delay:.15s; } .ds-typing span:nth-child(3) { animation-delay:.3s; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%,80%,100% { opacity:.25; transform:scale(.85); } 40% { opacity:1; transform:scale(1); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-typing span { animation:none; opacity:.55; transform:none; } }

components.name: Contact Card
components.description: A findings / routing card that renders inside the thread. Title, optional reason line, phone rows on the recessed faint fill, optional urgent hold-line in red.
components.html:

  • MWO Riyadh (Migrant Workers Office)+966 50 285 0944

Do not leave before speaking to the MWO.
components.css: .ds-card { align-self:flex-start; max-width:30rem; background:#fff; border-radius:24px; box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,31,31,.08),0 6px 18px rgba(31,31,31,.06); padding:1.15rem 1.3rem; font:400 1rem/1.55 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { margin:0 0 .3rem; font-weight:500; font-size:1.05rem; color:#1f1f1f; } .ds-card-reason { margin:0 0 .85rem; font-size:.9rem; color:#6e7370; } .ds-card-list { list-style:none; margin:0; padding:0; display:grid; gap:.5rem; } .ds-card-row { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:.15rem; padding:.7rem .9rem; border-radius:13px; background:#f1f1ee; } .ds-card-label { font-size:.82rem; color:#6e7370; } .ds-card-phone { font-weight:500; color:#1f5e4a; text-decoration:none; } .ds-card-hold { margin:.85rem 0 0; font-size:.88rem; color:#a30e1f; }

components.name: Case Panel
components.description: "What Gabay has understood" — the one panel of chrome the conversation adds. A dim title-bar button (chevron) over correctable claim rows and Safety-Flag pills (same rows as the old in-thread block; one-tap Conflict resolution lives here). Fixed top-right below the emergency pill above 1200px, with the thread reserving a matching right gutter; a centred pill that drops a floating sheet on tap at or below 1200px. Collapsed it is a pill, expanded a card. No flag red: Safety-Flag rows keep the tint-urgent wash. Shown only on the home screen, only with Case content, never during the Imminent Danger latch.
components.html:
months unpaid3

Safety notes

passport withheld
components.css: .ds-case { width:20rem; background:#fff; border-radius:24px; box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,31,31,.08),0 6px 18px rgba(31,31,31,.06); font:400 1rem/1.55 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; } .ds-case:not(.is-expanded) { border-radius:999px; } .ds-case-toggle { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:.5rem; width:100%; padding:.85rem 1rem .85rem 1.15rem; border:none; background:none; font:500 .8rem 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; color:#6e7370; text-align:left; cursor:pointer; transition:color .14s ease; } .ds-case-toggle:hover { color:#1f1f1f; } .ds-case-toggle:focus-visible { outline:3px solid rgba(31,94,74,.35); outline-offset:3px; } .ds-case-chevron { flex-shrink:0; display:grid; place-items:center; color:#8c918d; transition:transform .18s ease; } .ds-case-chevron svg { width:.9rem; height:.9rem; display:block; } .ds-case.is-expanded .ds-case-chevron { transform:rotate(180deg); } .ds-case-body { max-height:min(58vh,30rem); overflow-y:auto; padding:0 1.15rem 1.2rem; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:.6rem; transition:opacity .16s ease,transform .16s ease; } .ds-case:not(.is-expanded) .ds-case-body { max-height:0; padding-top:0; padding-bottom:0; opacity:0; transform:translateY(-.4rem); overflow:hidden; visibility:hidden; } .ds-case-claim { padding:.6rem .8rem; border-radius:13px; background:#f1f1ee; } .ds-case-field { display:block; font-size:.72rem; text-transform:capitalize; color:#6e7370; margin-bottom:.2rem; } .ds-case-value { font-size:.9rem; color:#1f1f1f; } .ds-case-h3 { margin:.3rem 0 0; font-size:.8rem; font-weight:500; color:#6e7370; } .ds-case-flag { padding:.5rem .75rem; border-radius:13px; background:rgba(206,17,38,.07); color:#a30e1f; font-size:.84rem; text-transform:capitalize; }

components.name: Emergency Pill
components.description: The calm-but-always-present emergency affordance, fixed to the top-right of every signed-in screen. Quiet white pill, flag-red dot and text; still renders a zero-model cached card.
components.css: .ds-emergency { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:.5rem; background:#fff; color:#ce1126; font:500 .86rem 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; padding:.6rem 1rem; border:none; border-radius:999px; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,31,31,.08),0 6px 18px rgba(31,31,31,.06); transition:box-shadow .14s ease; } .ds-emergency-dot { width:.5rem; height:.5rem; border-radius:50%; background:#ce1126; } .ds-emergency:hover { box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,31,31,.08),0 12px 34px rgba(31,31,31,.08); } .ds-emergency:focus-visible { outline:3px solid rgba(31,94,74,.35); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Rail Row
components.description: A conversation row in the left rail. Full pill, body text, transparent at rest, warm-grey on hover, darker + a pine dot when active.
components.css: .ds-rail-row { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:.6rem; padding:.62rem .85rem; border-radius:999px; color:#444746; font:400 .92rem 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-rail-row:hover { background:#e9e8e5; } .ds-rail-row--active { background:#e3e2df; color:#1f1f1f; font-weight:500; } .ds-rail-dot { width:.4rem; height:.4rem; border-radius:50%; background:#8c918d; } .ds-rail-row--active .ds-rail-dot { background:#1f5e4a; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: A form text field. Recessed faint fill, no border, small radius; focus is the pine ring, not a border shift.
components.css: .ds-input { width:100%; background:#f1f1ee; color:#1f1f1f; font:400 .95rem 'Figtree',system-ui,sans-serif; padding:.7rem .95rem; border:none; border-radius:13px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color:#6e7370; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline:3px solid rgba(31,94,74,.35); outline-offset:3px; }

narrative.northStar: One Surface, One Glow, One Bar
narrative.overview:
Gabay OFW is one calm surface an Overseas Filipino Worker talks to — often on a watched phone, in the middle of a bad situation, with a narrow window to act. The design borrows the shape of an assistant she already trusts how to use: a near-white ground, white lifted on soft shadow, a floating input at the foot of the screen. Everything that could be a border has been taken away; the only things that separate one region from another are a shadow and a stretch of empty space. Underneath that borrowed calm, the warmth is unmistakably hers — one diffuse glow drawn from the Philippine flag's blue, red and gold pools behind the greeting, the mark is an open hand holding a winding path drawn in one pine line, and the first word is "Kumusta". The aesthetic is borrowed; the brand is not.

The system is built by radical subtraction. There is one ground color, not a palette of surfaces. There is one glow, and it fades the moment a conversation starts so it never competes with what Gabay is saying. There is one input, and it never leaves the screen — findings and contact cards arrive inside the thread rather than on a screen she has to navigate to. The one panel of chrome the conversation adds is "What Gabay has understood": a quiet card top-right (a pill that drops a sheet on a narrow screen), collapsible and out of the way, so the record of her Case is one glance away without sitting in the reading column. Stillness is the feature. Type is large and light, weight 400 for even the biggest headings, so nothing on the page raises its voice.

Exactly one thing is allowed to break the calm: flag red. It marks the EMERGENCY exit, the delete-everything action, and an urgent finding — and nothing else, ever. Its rarity is what makes it legible under stress. The explicit anti-reference is a generic assistant blue: the glow is the flag's #0038a8, never a borrowed brand color, and the design never leans on another product's identity to feel trustworthy.
keyCharacteristics: Single near-white ground (#fbfbfa); white (#ffffff) only for surfaces that float
Zero borders in the current implementation — shadow and space do all separation
Figtree only, 300–500; headings are large, weight 400, tight-tracked
One flag-colored glow on the home screen, faded out once messaging begins
Flag red (#ce1126) reserved for urgent affordances, never decoration
One conversation, one composer that never leaves; no modes, no dashboard
Hand-and-path brand mark beside the wordmark; rotated pine square kept as the agent's speaker mark

rules.name: The One Red Line Rule
rules.body: Flag red appears on at most one element per screen and only ever means act now — EMERGENCY, delete-everything, or a single urgent finding line. Everything else, however important, stays ink. The red's scarcity is the signal; dilute it and the screen loses its one alarm.

rules.name: The Borrowed Light Rule
rules.body: Flag blue and flag gold are light, never material. They may only appear inside the .ph-glow gradient at low alpha. No fill, no text, no border, no icon uses them.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: #fbfbfa is the background of every screen. White is a signal that an element floats. A white section that isn't a card, input, message, or dialog is a bug.

rules.name: The Weight-400 Headline Rule
rules.body: Display and headline text is weight 400 — the body weight. If a heading is set in 600/700 to "make it a heading", the calm is broken. Reach for size and negative tracking instead.

rules.name: The Detected-Language Rule
rules.body: Copy is rendered in whichever of English, Filipino, or Cebuano Gabay detected — never chosen by the user. Institution names (DMW, OWWA, MWO, DOLE-SEnA) stay verbatim in every language so she can match them against a physical sign.

rules.name: The No-Line Rule
rules.body: Don't add a border to create separation. If two regions blur together, the fix is more space or a ground-shift, then a shadow — a 1px solid line is the wrong tool in this system. In dark this is load-bearing: shadow barely registers on black, so the ground-shift is the separation.

rules.name: The Glow-Recedes Rule
rules.body: The .ph-glow layer is decoration that must never compete with content. It is present and saturated on the empty home screen and animates to opacity: 0 (0.5s ease) the instant the thread has a message.

rules.name: The Quiet-Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion is state feedback, never spectacle — shadow and color shifts under 150ms, one glow fade, three pulsing loader dots. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the loader dots freeze to a static dimmed row, the glow fade and control transitions cut to instant, and smooth-scroll is dropped — the state change survives, the animation does not.

dos: Do put every new surface on the #fbfbfa ground and reserve white for things that genuinely float (cards, inputs, messages, dialogs, chips).
Do separate regions with space, then a one-shade ground shift, then a two-layer shadow — in that order.
Do keep the shell one screen tall and clipping — the page never scrolls; the rail is fixed and the message thread is the only scroll region (its own list is the rail's).

Do draw every glyph as an authored single-path SVG at one stroke weight — the compose, globe, chevron, sign-out, trash, photo, and send icons. Never a +, ×, or other typographic character standing in for an icon.
Do set headings at weight 400 and create hierarchy with size and negative tracking (-0.01em to -0.015em).
Do keep the reading column near 47rem and agent replies near 40rem, even on a wide screen.

Do render findings and contact cards as messages inside the thread; the composer must stay visible while she reads them. The Case is the one exception — it has its own quiet panel (see The Case panel).
Do keep the two marks in their lanes: the hand-and-path drawing beside the wordmark, the rotated pine square before Gabay's replies. Both always pine.

Do keep the emergency affordance always on screen and on the zero-model path, however quiet it looks — and first in the DOM, reachable by the skip link, so assistive-tech users reach it as fast as mouse users do.
Do give every interactive target ≥44px on a phone (the emergency pill first) and honor prefers-reduced-motion with a static alternative, not a blanket 0.01ms kill.
Do label every input with aria-label or <label> — a placeholder is not a name.
Do theme the browser surfaces from the palette: selection, caret, scrollbars, focus ring, and the theme-color meta pair.
Do keep every color a token — light and dark differ only in the :root values under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), never a per-component override.
Do mark non-English text (lang="tl" / lang="ceb") so a screen reader voices Filipino and Cebuano correctly — Gabay's reply, and each half of a bilingual opener chip.
donts: Don't add a 1px border to separate anything. The system has none.
Don't use flag red for anything that isn't act now — no red headings, no red dividers, no red hover states, no more than one red element per screen.
Don't fill a shape with flag blue or flag gold; they exist only inside the home glow at low alpha.
Don't let the glow sit under an active conversation — it fades to zero once the thread has a message.
Don't introduce a second font family or a bold heading weight.
Don't give Gabay's replies a bubble or a card; they are markless text after the pine square.
Don't shrink the brand mark below ~20px or drop it onto a transparent ground at tab size — use static/icon.svg instead.
Don't build a settings screen, a mode picker, or a separate findings page — one conversation, one composer, one Case.
Don't show a phone number, office name, distance, or citation that the server didn't send (ADR-0002).
